transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well… I guess I came because something’s been happening at home, and I didn’t want to make too big a deal out of it, but it’s been bothering me. I keep hearing voices, like clear as if somebody is standing right there in my little studio. They’ll say my name, and sometimes they say my work is being judged. But when I check, the house is quiet and nobody’s there. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right.
When you hear these voices, do they happen even when you’re not feeling particularly down or overly excited?

Yes… I think so. I mean, there was a time when I wasn’t all keyed up anymore, and my energy had kind of dropped back down. I was sleeping more regular again, so I figured it should’ve stopped, you know? But the voices still kept happening, and I still had that feeling that people were judging my work or kind of tracking what I was doing. It went on for a few weeks like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever felt like people are watching you or that your thoughts are being controlled, or have you had any unusual beliefs that others don’t seem to share?

Um… yes, I guess I have felt that way. I don’t want it to sound like I’m accusing people for no reason, but I got it in my head that the other home-care agency, and even some people from the library, were watching my paintings and my client papers.

It felt like they were trying to steal some chance that was supposed to be for me. People told me that didn’t really make sense, and I tried to listen, I did… but at the time I still felt like I knew they were doing it. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you ever had strong beliefs about things that others around you didn’t seem to agree with or understand, even when they tried to tell you otherwise?

Yes… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but I did have that. I got really sure that the other home-care agency, and some people from the library too, were watching my paintings and my client papers. Like they were trying to take some opportunity that was supposed to be mine.

People told me it didn’t make sense, and I tried to hear them, I really did… but at the time I still felt like I knew it was happening. Is that what you mean?

Have you ever had beliefs that something was happening—like people being after your work or watching you—that you held onto even when there was no clear evidence, and these beliefs weren’t just due to feeling down or overly anxious?

Yes… I think that’s right. I don’t like saying it like I was being unreasonable, but I did hold onto it.

I really believed that the other home-care agency, and some people from the library, were watching my paintings and my client papers… like they were trying to steal some chance that was supposed to be for me. People told me there wasn’t proof and that it didn’t make sense, and I tried to listen, but at the time I still felt like I knew they were doing it.

I wasn’t just sad or nervous when I believed it, if that helps.

Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing — maybe even times where others told you you were acting out of character or too excited?

Yes… I mean, I do have times like that. I try to use it in a good way, you know, not just make it sound bad.

I’ll get so much energy that I can’t really sit down. Like I’ll clean my whole kitchen, start three different paintings, crochet half a blanket, and then start rewriting care schedules all in the same night. It feels productive at the time, like I’m finally getting things done… but I guess it is a lot. Is that what you mean?

During the times you heard voices or felt people were watching you, did those experiences seem to match how you were feeling emotionally at the time—like if you were feeling down or especially irritable?

I think… yes, some of it did line up with when I was more keyed up, if that’s the right way to say it.

Like when I was only sleeping a few hours and really pushing these big art and care plans, that’s when I was also hearing the voices in the studio and feeling sure people were watching my work. I wasn’t trying to be dramatic about it — it just felt connected at the time, like everything was moving fast and important.
Have you ever experienced hearing voices or feeling like people were watching you when you weren’t feeling particularly down, overly excited, or emotionally elevated?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but there was a stretch after my energy had come down and I was sleeping more normal again where it didn’t fully stop.

The voices were still there sometimes, and I still had this feeling that people were judging my work or keeping track of what I was doing. It went on for several weeks, I guess. I wasn’t feeling especially up or really down then… at least not in the way I had been before. Does that answer it right?

Can you think of a time when you felt completely emotionally stable—neither especially up nor down—where you still experienced hearing voices or feeling like people were watching or judging your work?

Yes… I think that did happen. After my energy kind of dropped back down and I was sleeping more normally, I wasn’t feeling especially high or low, at least not that I could tell.

But the voices didn’t completely stop, and I still had that feeling like people were judging my work or keeping track of what I was doing. It kept going for several weeks. I know that probably sounds strange… I’m just trying to answer it the right way.

Have there been times when you felt down most of the day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or experienced other symptoms like changes in appetite or trouble concentrating, separate from the times you were feeling very energetic or having these experiences with voices and feeling watched?

I’m not sure I can separate it out that clearly. I mean, I’ve had days where I felt tired or kind of low, but I don’t know if it was most of the day or anything like that.

I don’t want to say yes if I’m not remembering it right. I haven’t really paid close attention to appetite or concentration separate from the other stuff. Sorry, is that okay?

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even when you weren’t having the experiences with voices or feeling watched?

I don’t know if I can honestly say that, no. I’ve had times where I felt low or didn’t feel like doing much, but I’m not sure it was two weeks straight, most of the day, nearly every day… especially separate from everything else.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just to be agreeable. I just haven’t tracked it that clearly. Is it okay if I say I’m not sure?

Have you ever had a time when you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day for at least two weeks, even when you weren’t hearing voices, feeling watched, or experiencing those high-energy periods?

I… I don’t think I can say yes to that clearly. I’ve felt down before, but the “most of the day, nearly every day for two weeks” part—I’m not sure.

And separating it from the voices or feeling watched or those high-energy times is hard for me. I don’t want to overstate it or give you the wrong impression. I’m sorry… is that the kind of answer you need?
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or depressed, not because of the voices or feeling watched, and it lasted for most of the day, nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m sorry, I still don’t think I can say that for sure. I’ve had low times, but whether it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks—and not because of the other stuff—I just don’t know.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was or give you an answer that isn’t accurate. Is it okay if I say I’m not sure?

Have you ever had a time when you felt down or depressed, not because of the voices or feeling watched, and during that time you also stopped enjoying things you usually like, or had trouble eating, sleeping, or focusing?

I’m not sure, doctor. I mean… I’ve had times where I didn’t feel like doing much, or I wasn’t eating or sleeping the best, but I don’t know if that was all together with feeling depressed like that, or if it was for long enough.

I don’t want to say yes if I’m just guessing. I guess I haven’t really kept track of it that way. Does that make sense?

Have you ever had a time when you felt down or depressed, not because of the voices or feeling watched, and during that time you also stopped enjoying things you usually like, or had trouble eating, sleeping, or focusing?

I don’t really know how to answer it better than… I can’t separate it out that cleanly. I’ve had times where I didn’t enjoy much, or my sleep and eating were off, but I don’t know if it was because I was depressed like you mean, or how long it lasted.

I’m sorry, I’m not trying to be difficult. I just don’t want to say yes and have it be wrong.

Can you think of a time when you felt down or depressed—not because of the voices or feeling watched—and during that time you also stopped enjoying things you usually like, or had trouble eating, sleeping, or focusing?

I wish I could give you a clearer answer, but I really can’t think of one that I’m sure about. I’ve had days where I was low and didn’t feel like myself, and maybe I didn’t enjoy things as much… but I don’t know if it was all connected the way you’re asking.

I don’t want to just agree and make it sound like something definite if I’m not positive. Is that okay to say?

Have you ever had a time when you felt down or depressed—not because of the voices or feeling watched—and during that time you also stopped enjoying things you usually like, or had trouble eating, sleeping, or focusing?

I’m sorry, doctor… I still can’t say for sure. I’ve had rough patches where I was kind of low or not taking care of myself great, but I don’t know if it was a real depressed period like you’re asking, separate from everything else.

I don’t want to give you a wrong answer just to be agreeable. Maybe the best I can say is I’m not sure.
